title: Java Collections and Kotlin Collections
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of java collections and kotlin collections using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates java collections and kotlin collections.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Java Collections and Kotlin Collections** as part of **Kotlin and Java Interoperability**. Select a collection by the invariants you need—ordering, uniqueness, key lookup, or indexed access—and check the cost of transformations. Use the subtopics—Collection Type Mapping, Mutable and Read-Only Views, Collection Interoperability Hazards—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Real projects depend on reliable error handling, modular organization, reproducible builds, and safe language boundaries. This lesson helps turn isolated syntax into maintainable applications.

items.title: Collection Type Mapping
items.text: Collection Type Mapping is best learned by tracing a small collection before and after the operation. Check ordering, duplicate handling, empty inputs, and whether the API returns a new value or mutates a mutable receiver.

items.title: Mutable and Read-Only Views
items.text: Mutable and Read-Only Views is one part of java collections and kotlin collections. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Collection Interoperability Hazards
items.text: Collection Interoperability Hazards means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet in a Kotlin/JVM console project and run the configured Gradle application task, or use the Kotlin Playground for examples that need no external dependencies.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A read-only collection reference proves that no code can mutate the underlying data.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
